_comment: Deterministic tier routing (D36). Data, not code: rules are tried in order, the first whose `when` matches wins. `when` keys: mechanical (Kind: mechanical AND passes the lint rules), critical_path (task is on the schedule's critical path), kind, tests (fast|slow), loc_lte, components_lte, time_lte (predicted min), focus_any (task has one of these Review Focus categories), focus_none (has none of them). A rule with `if_config` applies only when that top-level switch is true. Fixed in code, not configurable: a task on the critical path never gets the haiku tier. A rule may carry `min_first_time_pass` plus `evidence` {n, rate}: when the measured rate is below the minimum the band stays on the default tier (no evidence = not disabled). `stats_gate`: from history stats, a tier|band with at least min_n samples and a first-time pass rate below min_first_time_pass stays on the default tier. `prime` per tier: full (whole plan + spec sections), slim (rules, plan header, constraints, stable tasks' interfaces: the sonnet default) or mini (lane tier). A third tier = one more entry in `tiers` plus rules; nothing else changes. Thresholds from the mech-measure study drop into `rules` and `lane`.
